previous_last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now includes the active secondary (stage 2) injector duty cycle in the injector duty cycle cut protection. When staged injection is enabled, the higher of the primary and stage 2 duty cycles is compared against the instantaneous and sustained duty limits, and fuel resumes only once both active stages fall below 20 percent duty. The Injector Duty Cycle Cut page was updated to describe this behavior.

decisions.rationale: The injector duty cycle cut now also watches the secondary injector stage. With staged injection enabled, the higher of the primary and stage 2 duty cycles is used for both the instantaneous and sustained limits, and the cut releases only when both active stages drop below 20 percent duty. Tuners running staged injection should check that the duty limits suit the secondary injectors as well, since a stage 2 excursion can now cut fuel even when the primary stage looks safe. With staged injection disabled, behavior is unchanged. This is a firmware logic change; it has not been validated on an engine.
evidence: firmware/controllers/limp_manager.cpp: updateCutsInjectorDuty now takes std::max(getInjectorDutyCycle(rpm), getInjectorDutyCycleStage2(rpm)) when engineConfiguration->enableStagedInjection is set

decisions.rationale: Integration merge of the secondary injector duty fix. Its only content is the child commit already documented, and the merge introduces no additional user-facing change.
evidence: Merge commit dfeba99a with parents 15b1ee02 and 9695e6e9; changed paths are the same limp_manager.cpp and test_limp.cpp covered by the child commit
No conflict-resolution changes beyond the child commit's diff

last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now enforces the antilag maximum activation duration as a continuous timeout. Antilag stays active only while all arming conditions are met and the elapsed time since arming is below ALSMaxDuration; once the timeout expires it stays off until the arming conditions clear and re-apply. A non-positive ALSMaxDuration now inhibits antilag, and the default duration changed from 3.5 to 3 seconds.

decisions.rationale: Antilag activation is now limited by a continuous timer. The timer starts on a false-to-true transition of the arming conditions and antilag turns off when elapsed time reaches ALSMaxDuration. After a timeout, antilag does not restart while the arming conditions remain true; they must clear and re-apply. Setting ALSMaxDuration to zero or a negative value now prevents antilag from activating, so tuners must use a positive duration. The default ALSMaxDuration changed from 3.5 to 3 seconds; existing tunes keep their stored value. Verify the duration and arming conditions on the bench before relying on antilag.
evidence: firmware/controllers/algo/antilag_system.cpp: update() adds durationValid = ALSMaxDuration > 0, resets m_maxDurationTimer on eligible && !m_wasEligible, and sets ALSTimerCondition from elapsed seconds < ALSMaxDuration
firmware/controllers/algo/antilag_system.h: adds private Timer m_maxDurationTimer and bool m_wasEligible
unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_antilag.cpp: new tests for expiry boundary, no re-arm after timeout, re-arm after arming condition clears, non-positive duration inhibits, and disabled inhibits

decisions.rationale: Integration merge of the antilag timeout fix. It adds no user-facing change beyond the child commit already documented.
